identity.name: AutoGen
identity.one_liner: Multi-agent AI framework from Microsoft Research for building conversational agent systems with AgentChat, Core API, and Extensions.
identity.short_description: AutoGen is Microsoft Research's open-source framework for building multi-agent AI systems. It provides three layers — AgentChat for quick prototyping, Core API for fine-grained control, and Extensions for ecosystem integrations — giving developers a flexible foundation for agent collaboration patterns.

positioning.why_it_matters: AutoGen matters because it comes from one of the most well-resourced AI research labs in the world and is designed around the principle that agent conversations are the fundamental primitive for multi-agent systems. Its layered architecture lets developers start simple and add complexity as needed.
best_for: Research teams studying agent collaboration patterns and emergent behavior
Engineers who need fine-grained control over agent state, messaging, and orchestration
not_for: Developers who only need a single-agent terminal coding tool
Teams looking for a drag-and-drop workflow builder with a visual UI

core_strengths.title: Layered architecture
core_strengths.description: AutoGen provides three layers: AgentChat for rapid prototyping, Core API for fine-grained control, and Extensions for ecosystem integrations.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Developers can start with the simplest layer and add complexity as their needs grow, without rewriting their codebase.

core_strengths.title: Conversation-centric design
core_strengths.description: Agent conversations are the fundamental primitive. Agents collaborate through structured message passing with built-in conversation patterns.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Conversation-centric design makes it natural to model complex multi-agent interactions like debates, reviews, and iterative refinement.

core_strengths.title: Microsoft ecosystem integration
core_strengths.description: Backed by Microsoft Research with deep integration into Azure AI services and the broader Microsoft developer ecosystem.
core_strengths.why_it_matters: Teams already on Azure get first-class support, and the Microsoft backing means long-term maintenance and enterprise readiness.

seo_article.intro: AutoGen is Microsoft Research's framework for building multi-agent AI systems. It treats agent conversations as the fundamental building block and provides a layered architecture that scales from quick prototypes to production systems.
seo_article.what_it_is: AutoGen is an open agent resource to evaluate by action surface: what software it can operate, which tools or browser steps it touches, and how much supervision it needs before it can run real work.
seo_article.why_it_matters: Multi-agent systems are becoming the standard approach for complex AI tasks, but building them from scratch is hard. AutoGen provides the primitives — agent registration, message routing, conversation management, state handling — so developers can focus on designing agent behaviors rather than infrastructure.

alternatives.title: Use CrewAI for a more accessible API
alternatives.summary: AutoGen offers more control and flexibility. CrewAI has a gentler learning curve and more intuitive role-based design.

alternatives.title: Use a single agent for simple tasks
alternatives.summary: If your task doesn't require multiple specialized agents, a single-agent tool like Claude Code or Aider will be simpler and faster.
